proof_summary: For integers above the respective thresholds, positivity supplies primes whose parity-specialized representation is directly a Goldbach decomposition (even case) or a Lemoine decomposition (odd case), while explicit finite tables of prime decompositions handle all smaller admissible integers. For any bound, applying the even case to \(2m\) with \(m=\max(4007,a+7)\) yields primes \(2m-q-6\) and \(2m-q\), and the inequality \(q<m\) makes this cousin-prime pair exceed the bound, proving infinitude.
